q1: SELECT DISTINCT F.ORIGIN_CITY, F.DEST_CITY, F.ACTUAL_TIME FROM FLIGHTS AS F JOIN (SELECT A.ORIGIN_CITY, MAX(A.ACTUAL_TIME) AS MAX_TIME FROM FLIGHTS AS A GROUP BY A.ORIGIN_CITY) AS X ON F.ORIGIN_CITY = X.ORIGIN_CITY AND F.ACTUAL_TIME = X.MAX_TIME
q2: SELECT S.ORIGIN_CITY, F2.DEST_CITY, MAX(F2.ACTUAL_TIME) FROM (SELECT F1.ORIGIN_CITY, MAX(F1.ACTUAL_TIME) AS MAX_TIME FROM FLIGHTS AS F1 GROUP BY F1.ORIGIN_CITY) AS S JOIN FLIGHTS AS F2 ON S.ORIGIN_CITY = F2.ORIGIN_CITY AND F2.ACTUAL_TIME = S.MAX_TIME GROUP BY S.ORIGIN_CITY, F2.DEST_CITY
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT F.ORIGIN_CITY, F.DEST_CITY, F.ACTUAL_TIME FROM FLIGHTS AS F JOIN (SELECT A.ORIGIN_CITY, MAX(A.ACTUAL_TIME) AS MAX_TIME FROM FLIGHTS AS A GROUP BY A.ORIGIN_CITY) AS X ON F.ORIGIN_CITY = X.ORIGIN_CITY AND F.ACTUAL_TIME = X.MAX_TIME
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT S.ORIGIN_CITY, F2.DEST_CITY, MAX(F2.ACTUAL_TIME) FROM (SELECT F1.ORIGIN_CITY, MAX(F1.ACTUAL_TIME) AS MAX_TIME FROM FLIGHTS AS F1 GROUP BY F1.ORIGIN_CITY) AS S JOIN FLIGHTS AS F2 ON S.ORIGIN_CITY = F2.ORIGIN_CITY AND F2.ACTUAL_TIME = S.MAX_TIME GROUP BY S.ORIGIN_CITY, F2.DEST_CITY
counterexample: INSERT INTO FLIGHTS (FID, ORIGIN_CITY, DEST_CITY, ACTUAL_TIME) VALUES (1, 1, 2, 100), (2, 1, 3, 100), (3, 2, 4, 150), (4, 2, 5, 150);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 selects the distinct origin and destination cities for the flights that have the maximum actual time for each origin city, while Q2 selects the origin city, destination city, and the maximum actual time for each origin city, grouping by both origin city and destination city. This difference in grouping can lead to different results.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when there are multiple flights with the same maximum actual time for the same origin city, but different destination cities.
